setup.zh: 你浮上水面的时候，日头已经落尽了。那口鼎跟着你浮了上来，越浮越小，落在你手心里，沉甸甸的，暖的。
setup.en: By the time you surface, the sun has set. The cauldron rises with you, smaller and smaller, and lands in your palm, heavy and warm.

recap.zh: 第一鼎归来，木牌亮了第二条尾巴；柳树底下站着一个白衣人：「太一宫，赵昂。」「因为天下，该归于一。」他看见了你掌心的印：「烙上了，就是宫里的。」
recap.en: The first cauldron came home and a second tail lit on the token; under the willow stood a man in white: "Taiyi Palace. Zhao Ang." "Because all under heaven should be one." He saw the mark in your palm: "Burned in, it is the Palace's."

zh: 木牌上，第二条尾巴亮了。
en: A cauldron the size of a palm, warm.
On the token, a second tail alight.
Under the willow, someone in white.

story.zh:
小满浮上水面的时候，日头已经落尽了，天边只剩一抹暗红。那口鼎跟着他浮了上来，越浮越小，浮出水面时只有巴掌大，落在他手心里，沉甸甸的，暖的。

胸口的木牌烫得前所未有，他低头一看，木牌上那只蜷着的小狐狸，九条尾巴里，第二条亮了。
story.en:
When Xiaoman surfaced, the sun had set, with only a streak of dark red left at the sky's edge. The cauldron rose with him, growing smaller, and when it broke the surface it was the size of a palm; it landed in his hand, heavy and warm.

The token at his chest burned as never before; he looked down, and of the nine tails of the little curled fox on it, a second was alight.

exits.means: takes up the cauldron, keeps it, faces the stranger in white

story.zh:
那人站在岸边一株老柳树底下，一身白衣，腰悬长剑，正是方才上游柳树底下那一个。

他的目光，落在小满手心里那口巴掌大的鼎上，开口第一句话，却是：「多谢。」

小满一怔：「谢什么？」那人道：「二十年，宫里请不动他。你一个上午，就把他请上来了。」他往前走了两步，月光照在他腰间那柄剑的剑鞘上，剑鞘头上刻着一个记号：一个圆圈，圈里一横。「太一宫，赵昂。」

太一宫，这三个字小满头一回听见。可那记号他认得：马三嘴里那些「太华山上的仙长」，马小宝腰里那面「白衣仙长留下的」镜子，开山门那天山脚下拿银子换孩子的白衣人，原来都是这一家。眼前这一个，脚下没声，是筑了基的；听那口气，不是跑腿的。

赵昂这才正眼看了他，道：「因为天下，该归于一。」

小满怀里的银月，猛地一颤。

「在九天之上。」银月一字一字地道，「那道光劈下来的时候，光里那个声音，说的就是这一句：天下，该归于一。」

他的眼睛往下一落，落在小满托着鼎的那只手上。鼎底下，掌心里，那个印露了出来。赵昂看着它，看了很久，脸上第一回有了一点东西，说不清是惊，还是别的什么。他道：「宫里的印。」顿了一顿，「烙上了，就是宫里的。」

「锁儿。是你们的人么？」

赵昂没有答。月光底下，他那张好看的脸，一点一点地白了下去。过了很久，他才道：「……宫里的孩子，没有名字。」

赵昂盯着他，按在剑柄上的手松了又紧，终于放了下来，道：「今日冰夷护着你。我不跟一条河打架。」
story.en:
The man stood under an old willow at the water's edge, all in white, a long sword at his waist — the same one who had stood under the willows upstream.

His eyes fell on the palm-sized cauldron in Xiaoman's hand, and the first thing he said was: "Thank you."

Xiaoman was startled: "For what?" The man said: "For twenty years the Palace couldn't get him to come up. You did it in one morning." He took two steps forward; moonlight fell on the scabbard at his waist, and on its tip was a mark: a circle, with one bar inside it. "Taiyi Palace. Zhao Ang."

Taiyi Palace — Xiaoman had never heard the name. But the mark he knew: the "immortal masters from Mount Taihua" Ma San always bragged of, the mirror at Ma Xiaobao's waist "left by the Immortal Master in white", the man in white at the foot of the mountain on opening day trading silver for a child — all one house. This one walked without a sound and had laid his Foundation; by his tone, he was no errand boy.

Only then did Zhao Ang really look at him: "Because all under heaven should be one."

Yinyue, in Xiaoman's arms, gave a violent start.

"High in the ninth heaven," Yinyue said, word by word. "When that light struck down, the voice in the light said exactly this: all under heaven should be one."

His eyes dropped to the hand that held the cauldron. Under the cauldron, in the palm, the brand showed. Zhao Ang looked at it a long time, and for the first time something showed in his face — surprise, or something else. He said: "The Palace's seal." A pause. "Burned in, it is the Palace's."

"Suo'er. Was he one of yours?"

Zhao Ang did not answer. In the moonlight his handsome face slowly went white. After a long while he said: "…The Palace's children have no names."

Zhao Ang stared at him, his hand on the hilt tightening and loosening, and at last he let it go: "Today Bingyi guards you. I don't fight a river."

exits.means: hesitates, asks what will happen, wants to wait

text.zh: 它在你掌心里，一明，一暗，像在很慢地呼吸。
text.en: It lies in your palm, light and dark, as if breathing very slowly.
